Fourteen comments

Sets

My father and uncle. fiddle and flute player from Kenilworth, Ontario, play this tune in a set beginning with the Daisy Field, then the Mountain Top, then the Five Mile Chase.

↳ Posted by dances with swords on December 10th, 2004.

A very old tune - it is printed in Howe’s 1000 Jigs and Reels, which is now available in reprint from Mel Bay, edited by Pat Sky - some of the tunes in this book (which, like the later Ryan’s Mammoth Collection, was compiled and printed in Boston in the mid-late 19th century) have instructions for dancers, and the one for this tune starts out with this interesting comment:

“The Scotch are indefatigable when dancing this Reel; they seem almost intoxicated with it - they snap their fingers -- throw their arms and feet in the air -- screech out - and make such quick, and difficult steps, that the eyes have trouble following them.”

↳ Posted by Lucy Rietmann on March 16th, 2005.

More titles

This tune appears no fewer than three times in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection (c. 1886), under the titles Lady Gardner’s Reel, Parnell’s Reel, and Corporal Casey’s Fancy. Also appears in the Roche Collection (c. 1926) as The Wild Fire Chase. Evidently a very popular tune!

↳ Posted by rwwt on October 27th, 2010.

The Five Mile Chase, X:6

This setting appears in O’Neill’s Waifs and Strays of Gaelic Melody, 1922, no. 207, as Four-Hand Reel.

↳ Posted by Moxhe on November 13th, 2015.

Re: The Five Mile Chase/ Yellow Hair’d Laddie

This reel appears in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection under at least four different titles including Yellow Hair’d Laddie (#277). The practice of (inadvertently) putting in duplicate settings of tunes has been repeated by subsequent collectors.

↳ Posted by brailsford on July 30th, 2023.

The Five Mile Chase AKA Yellow Hair’d Laddie, X:10

The setting of “Yellow Hair’d Laddie” in Ryan’s, mentioned above.

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on March 29th, 2024.

The Five Mile Chase, X:11

This setting from a recording of Mrs. Molly Myers Murphy of Glencollins, Ballydesmond, Co. Cork. She likely got it from Tom Billy Murphy, the blind fiddle master that taught her during her youth in Co. Kerry.

↳ Posted by Thady Quill on December 17th, 2024.

The Five Mile Chase, X:12

I heard Graham Guerin and Paraic MacDonnacha play this setting on a recording from a friend. Nice how they change the tonality of the tune in by using E’s and G’s instead of F’s and D’s.

↳ Posted by Thady Quill on December 17th, 2024.
